case_notes.generic_target: ERROR with UNSUPPORTED_SYMBOL_FORM by design. The target is written as the generic form `ParseAny[T]`; the linker method has no verified rule for mapping generic symbols to binary names (they appear as instantiation-specific names such as `ParseAny[go.shape.string]`), so it refuses instead of guessing.
case_notes.inlined_small: Flips to ABSENT with inlining enabled. `ParseTiny` is a one-line function; the compiler inlines it into main and the linker then drops the unused out-of-line copy. This is why scoring uses only the `-gcflags=all=-l` run (ADR-013).
case_notes.method_value_receiver: Flips to ABSENT with inlining enabled. The target `Impl.Run` is a one-line method; when it is inlined at its only (static) call site and no interface or reflection use keeps it, the linker drops the method symbol. Explanation inferred from the code; the binary was not disassembled.
case_notes.method_pointer_receiver: Flips to ABSENT with inlining enabled, for the same reason as `method_value_receiver` (one-line `(*PImpl).Run`, static call only). Explanation inferred from the code; the binary was not disassembled.
case_notes.unsafe_func_pointer: Not a real test of `unsafe`. The program takes the function value `vulnlib.Parse` before converting it through `unsafe.Pointer`, and taking a function value keeps the symbol in the binary, so the result says nothing about `unsafe`-hidden calls (CP1 review note).
case_notes.build_tag_excluded: Trivial agreement: the excluded file is never compiled, so no method can see the call.
case_notes.test_file_only: Trivial agreement: `_test.go` files are not part of the built program.
